routing_policy.note: Owner directives 2026-10-10: Space Bunny MAX is the default and only active OpenCode executor for every lane (/oc, /bunny, /bunny-review, the launcher, the opencode-subagent MCP and every OpenCode subagent), served by OpenCode Zen as opencode/space-bunny-free. DeepSeek v4.1 Flash MAX is SUSPENDED and never selected, not even as a fallback. OpenCode Go ids are not admitted. Historical references to DeepSeek or opencode-go/space-bunny are provenance only.
routing_policy.selection_authority: Every run resolves the space-bunny profile. Re-activating DeepSeek needs a new direct Owner instruction recorded in this registry.

resolution_policy.note: Exactly two logical executor profiles. All runtime model IDs below map to one of them; there is no third logical executor and no non-Bunny or cross-family substitute. Space Bunny resolves only after live pinned-CLI catalog inspection of the Zen provider: its single admitted id must be listed, otherwise fail closed. OpenCode Go Space Bunny ids are not admitted.

cross_executor_review_policy.note: MATERIAL implementation workstreams require a fresh-context READ-ONLY Space Bunny MAX review of the exact validated implementation SHA and TREE before PR_READY or COMPLETE. Only the top-level read-only /bunny-review lane (foundry-reviewer) can carry verifiable review evidence; a writable top-level run or a subagent it dispatches never satisfies the gate. While DeepSeek is SUSPENDED the implementation executor is also Space Bunny, so the review is same-model and its independence rests on the fresh context and read-only lane alone (review_independence). A later generated-state-only checkpoint may be NON_MATERIAL and preserves the reviewed validated implementation identity without claiming the later state commit was reviewed.
